newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 92 n/c on last week

AMLC COMMENTARY: Prices on the U.S. beef market were generally lower this week, the combined result of relatively poor retail beef movement and slow export sales. U.S. domestic grinding beef values were down for the week ended Thursday and this depressed the market for imported product. U.S. domestic 90CL boneless beef lost 1.0 cent to 81c/lb, 85CL beef trimmings fell 2.0 cents and frozen 50CL beef trim fell 3.0 cents to 56 c/lb.
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 142 +7 on last week

The impact on Australian lean grinding beef prices was less marked with increases evident for one or two cuts. Most prices were unchanged or a little lower, however, and a 7.0 cent fall was recorded for insides to 106c/lb, partly reflecting sharp declines in U.S. domestic prices.

In Japan, consumer demand has started to pick up as winter approaches with retailers reporting that sales of thinly sliced beef and steaks have improved. Prices on the wholesale markets continued to improve for most cuts this week. The strength of the wholesale market is very ecouraging but it must be kept in mind that most of this movement is the result of the low level
of chilled beef imports over the past couple of months. The current shortage of supply has been the major reason for the price rises rather than strong end-user demand.

In the Australian cattle market, widespread rains in the eastern states resulted in a fall in cattle yardings in Queensland and prices of between 5.0 and 10 A.cents per kg. Cattle prices also rose in New South Wales and Victoria.
